properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 4 at 1:41PM EDT until September 4 at 2:30PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
SVRRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston West Virginia has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Meigs County in southeastern Ohio...
Southeastern Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Northwestern Wirt County in northwestern West Virginia...
North central Jackson County in northwestern West Virginia...
Southwestern Wood County in northwestern West Virginia...

* Until 230 PM EDT.

* At 140 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Lubeck to 8 miles southeast of Athens, moving
southeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Parkersburg, Coolville, Forked Run State Park, Tuppers Plains,
Lubeck, Washington, Mineralwells, Belleville, Reedsville,
Blennerhassett, Greencastle, and Davisville.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 77 in West Virginia between mile markers 163 and 173.
Route 50 in West Virginia between mile markers 1 and 5.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 4:29PM CDT until September 4 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Hardin County in southeastern Texas...
Northwestern Jefferson County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 428 PM CDT, Gauge reports and emergency management are
reporting flooding continuing. Flooding is already occurring in
the warned area.
- Flood water are moving down Village Creek, Little Pine Island
Bayou and Pine Island Bayou.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lumberton, Silsbee, Kountze, Sour Lake, Saratoga, Wildwood,
Thicket, Bevil Oaks, Honey Island, Village Mills, Batson and
Votaw.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 4 at 12:42PM CDT until September 4 at 1:45PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
At 1242 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Poplarville, Mcneil and Crossroads.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 4 at 1:34PM EDT until September 4 at 2:15PM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
SVRILN

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Eastern Delaware County in central Ohio...
Northern Licking County in central Ohio...

* Until 215 PM EDT.

* At 133 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Delaware to near Mount Vernon, moving southeast
at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to trees and power lines.

* Locations impacted include...
Delaware, Johnstown, Sunbury, Utica, Ashley, Radnor, Galena,
Hartford, St. Louisville, Interstate 71 at US Route 36/State Route
37, Alum Creek State Park, Delaware State Park, Fredonia, Olive
Green, US Route 62 at State Route 661, Purity, Center Village,
Fallsburg, Leonardsburg, and Kilbourne.

This includes I-71 in Ohio between mile markers 126 and 138.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Large hail, damaging wind, and continuous cloud to ground lightning
are occurring with these storms. Move indoors immediately. Lightning
is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

To report severe weather, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 4 at 10:45AM CDT until September 5 at 12:44PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Menard Creek near Rye affecting Polk, Hardin and Liberty Counties.

For the Menard Creek...including Rye...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, moderate lowland flooding begins as
low-lying areas along the creek are inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 24.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:15 AM CDT Friday was 28.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 11.1 feet
Wednesday morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 24.6
feet on 03/12/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1045 PM CDT.
